title: What plan lets one player always win the grid challenge?
description: On a six by six grid, two players take turns covering two touching squares with a line, and the player who cannot place a line loses. The second player wins by placing the half turn picture of each line about the centre, which is always free. Keeko raises the doubt that a mirror picture across the middle line can be used as the reply.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the board matches itself after a half turn about its centre, the second player can always answer a move with the half turn copy of it. Watch for students who reply with a mirror picture, which fails when the first line lies across the middle line.

source: Draw a 6 by 6 grid. Two players take turns covering two adja
video_script.why: The child uses a half turn about the centre of a grid to find a plan that the second player can always follow to win.
video_script.substitution: The book's own six by six grid and its rule of covering two touching squares with a line.
video_script.anchor: the book's 6 by 6 grid, where two players take turns covering two touching squares with a line placed flat or upright
video_script.wrong_answer: put the mirror picture of the line across the middle line
video_script.wrong_move: replies with the mirror picture of the first line across a middle line, which lands on the same squares when the first line lies across the middle line

final_answer.value: the second player wins: after each move of the first player, place the half turn (180°) copy of that line about the centre of the grid
final_answer.spoken: the second player wins, by placing the half turn copy of each line of the first player about the centre of the grid

never_show: a reply that lies on the same squares as the first line
a line placed over the centre point of the grid
maths_rules: the grid is 6 squares by 6 squares; its centre is the corner point where 4 squares meet
a line covers 2 touching squares, so it can never cover the centre point
half turn = 180 degrees about the centre; the square in row r and column c goes to row 7 - r and column 7 - c
a square and its half turn partner are never touching: the rows differ by an odd number of at least 1 and so do the columns, so they are at least 2 steps apart
so the half turn copy of a line never overlaps the line itself
after each reply the lines on the grid come in half turn pairs, so the squares of the next copy are free
the second player always has a reply, so the first player runs out of moves first and loses
slip: the mirror picture of a flat line over the two middle squares of a row, across the vertical middle line, lands on the same squares, so there is no free place
video_script.design: One idea: a half turn about the centre sends every line to a free place. One grid, the first player's lines in teal and the second player's lines in amber, the centre dot in red.

<bookmark mark='lines'/>Players take turns drawing a line over two touching squares. The line can lie flat or stand upright, and lines cannot overlap.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The player who cannot place a line loses. What plan can one use to win?
